questions.prompt: Claude's rate limiter uses the token bucket algorithm. What does that mean for your capacity?

options.text: It refills all the way at the start of each new minute.
options.explanation: That describes a fixed window. The Claude docs say capacity is not reset at fixed intervals.

options.text: It refills continuously, up to your maximum limit.
options.explanation: Right. The docs say capacity is continuously replenished up to your maximum, not reset at fixed intervals.

options.text: It counts only tokens, so request counts never matter.
options.explanation: Claude limits requests per minute as well as input and output tokens per minute.

questions.prompt: You hit a Gemini rate limit and create a second API key in the same Google Cloud project. What changes?

options.text: Nothing, because Gemini limits are applied per project, not per key.
options.explanation: Right. The Gemini docs say rate limits are applied per project, not per API key.

options.text: The requests-per-minute limit doubles for the project.
options.explanation: Limits belong to the project. A new key in the same project shares them.

options.text: Only the daily request quota doubles, and per-minute limits stay.
options.explanation: Neither limit is per key. Daily quotas also belong to the project and reset at midnight Pacific time.

questions.prompt: A Claude model has a 2,000,000 ITPM limit. With an 80% cache hit rate, about how many input tokens per minute can you process?

options.explanation: Only the 20% uncached share counts toward the limit. So the total is 5 times 2 million, which is 10 million, not 20.
That counts only the cached share. The 2 million uncached tokens are processed as well.
Right. The docs' example: 2 million uncached plus 8 million cached, because cached tokens do not count toward the limit.
